section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the simple level of selfhood is already rectified through the repentance of Elul, while the repentance of Shabbos Shuvah addresses the most subtle selfhood, requiring the revelation of the Essence of Ein Sof.
section.t: And one may add,
that the matter of selfhood
(of "there is one who loves")
in its simple sense is already rectified through the service of teshuvah of the month of Elul,
"And she wept for her father and her mother for a month of days"64
which refers to the month of Elul
(as is brought in the writings of the Arizal65),
the month of mercy,
when the king is in the field66,
and particularly in the days after the 18th of Elul, which brings life into all the matters of the month of Elul67,
and especially in the days of Selichos when we say "To You,
Hashem, is righteousness, and to us is shame of face,"
the self-nullification of the awe of shame, which is the awe of exaltation in the most supreme degree69,
and especially on Erev Rosh Hashanah, whose matter is
(as its name, Erev Rosh Hashanah, indicates)
preparation for Rosh Hashanah,
and especially on Rosh Hashanah itself, when the service is the acceptance of the yoke of the kingdom of heaven,
"Make Me king over you"70.
And the teshuvah of Shabbos Shuvah is regarding selfhood as it is in its ultimate subtlety.
Therefore, it is explained in Likkutei Torah that the explanation of "Shuvah Yisrael ad Hashem Elokecha"
[which we say on Shabbos Shuvah]
is that Hashem should be only Elokim and a contraction relative to the Essence of Ein Sof,
for in order to negate selfhood in its ultimate subtlety, it is specifically through the revelation of the Essence of Ein Sof, which is above Hashem.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section details the three levels of teshuvah—Sur MeRa, Aseh Tov, and Bakesh Shalom—corresponding to Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah, and explains their connection to the verses in Hoshea.
section.t: And after71 saying "Shuvah Yisrael etc., for you have stumbled in your iniquity,"
which is the teshuvah of "Sur MeRa" (turn from evil)
[as it is in the level of Yisrael],
it adds "Take words with you and return to Hashem,
say to Him, 'All sin forgive,'"
these two teshuvos are the teshuvah of "Aseh Tov" (do good) and the teshuvah of "Bakesh Shalom" (seek peace).
And this will be understood by prefacing what is explained in Likkutei Torah72
that the three teshuvos of Sur MeRa, Aseh Tov, and Bakesh Shalom correspond to the three levels of Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah.
The teshuvah of Sur MeRa
(which is regarding sin and iniquity)
is in the level of Nefesh.
For the matter of sin and iniquity applies only in the level of Nefesh, as it is written73
"The soul that sins"74.
And also the teshuvah
(of Sur MeRa)
is in the level of Nefesh,
for the teshuvah of Sur MeRa is that one accepts upon himself the yoke of the kingdom of heaven and the yoke of mitzvos
[not to rebel against His kingship, G-d forbid, nor to transgress the king's commands75],
and the matter of accepting the yoke is in the level of Nefesh.
The teshuvah of Aseh Tov,
which is regarding the absence of arousal of love and awe
[for the drawing down that comes through the performance of mitzvos
(Aseh Tov)
is through love and awe, which are the wings by which one ascends above76,
and also the perfection of the performance of mitzvos themselves is specifically through love77],
is in the level of Ruach,
for the emotions of the heart
(love and awe)
are the level of Ruach.
And the teshuvah of Bakesh Shalom,
which is regarding the absence of engagement in Torah with understanding and comprehension,
and more specifically—the teshuvah regarding the absence of comprehension of G-dliness,
and primarily regarding the fact that the G-dly matter is not felt in his mind
(for even when he contemplates a G-dly matter, the matter is not felt in his mind),
is in the level of Neshamah,
"The Neshamah of Shaddai gives them understanding"78,
and this is why regarding the teshuvah of Aseh Tov it is written "Take words with you," and regarding the teshuvah of Bakesh Shalom it is written "Say to Him,"
for speech
(words)
pertains to the emotions
(for speech is the breath that issues from the heart79),
and therefore it is the level of Ruach,
"a speaking spirit"80,
and "saying" which is in the heart81,
thought,
is82
the level of Neshamah.
And this is also the meaning of "Say to Him, 'Kol'" (all),
"Kol" being an expression of inclusion,
for
(Bakesh)
Shalom is the matter of inclusion.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the teshuvah of the Neshamah level elevates the Nefesh and Ruach, even in their own places, which is why it says "forgive sin" regarding this teshuvah.
section.t: And what is said in this teshuvah
(of the level of Neshamah)
"Tisa Avon" (forgive sin),
will be understood based on what is said in the Zohar83
(which is said in the Vidui confession)
"Their holy Nefesh, their holy Ruach, their holy Neshamah, Holy of Holies,"
that the reason the Neshamah is called "Holy of Holies" is because it includes within itself also the holiness of Nefesh and Ruach.
And since the Nefesh and Ruach as they are included in the Neshamah are on a more elevated level
[similar to the Chayah and Yechidah in man, which are above the Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah,
and likewise regarding the worlds of BYA within Atzilus,
and similarly regarding the Sefiros of Atzilus as they are hidden in that which is above Atzilus],
therefore, through the teshuvah of the Neshamah, an elevation is effected also in the Nefesh and Ruach,
and not only as they are included in the Neshamah, but also as they are in their own place.
And therefore, regarding the teshuvah of the level of Neshamah it says "Tisa Avon" (forgive sin),
for through this teshuvah,
an elevation is effected also in the teshuvah of Sur MeRa.
